guide_title: FC Barcelona Museum · Spotify Camp Nou

voices.1: en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural (chosen voice), base rate -8%, directed per passage (render_edge.py)

tracks.room: Outside the museum · on Av. de Joan XXIII, by the long building with the ridged roof beside the round Palau Blaugrana, out of the way of its door
tracks.title: Welcome to the Barça Museum
tracks.where: Outside, on Avinguda de Joan XXIII, by the long building with the ridged roof that stands beside the round Palau Blaugrana; stop out of the way of the museum's door.
tracks.what: The honesty frame (F17.8 OK OFF: no stadium interior on this ticket; ROUTE §1.1 OFF-AJ); the museum's temporary home in the old ice rink (F16.11 OK OFF; F17.3) [RL]; what the visit gives: the trophies with all five men's European Cups (F11.10 OK OFF), the history, Messi's golden balls (F16.17 OK OFF), the round room (F16.13–16.14 OK OFF), the models, the viewpoint (F17.4 OK OFF); the route in one breath [RL] (ROUTE §0.3, O3); practical lines (headphones; "about an hour" ROUTE §1.1 OFF; the epilepsy and photosensitivity warning F16.19 OK OFF; offline, COMP §4.2-5); the three lengths as Lead's decision 1 words them; the forward pointer answered by 034.
tracks.listen: An honest welcome: what this ticket shows and what it doesn't, how the visit runs, and how long each version takes.

tracks.room: The campus · where the stadium is in view over the lower buildings
tracks.title: The campus · 909 days away
tracks.where: On the campus, a short walk from the museum, at a spot where the stadium shows over the lower buildings.
tracks.what: The return on Saturday 22 Nov 2025, 4–0 v Athletic Club, 45,157 under a first licence of 45,401, 909 days away (F15.6 OK OFF [O7]); the last match 28 May 2023 v Mallorca (F6.15 OK OFF); the works under way within days, the pitch first (F15.4 OK OFF [O56]); two seasons at Montjuïc (F15.5 OK OFF [O29]); Lewandowski the first goal, Lamine Yamal the first assist with the outside of his foot for Ferran Torres, who scored twice (F15.7 OK OFF [O8]); nine Catalan players, the most at a home game since 1937 (F15.8 OK OFF [O7]); [RL] look at the stadium, top unfinished; DATED: about 62,000 since March 2026 with the Gol Nord open (F15.9 SEC [S3]; OFF statement 10 Mar 2026); Gol 1957 (ROUTE A.5 OFF); payoff as PLAN.
tracks.listen: The night the team came home after two and a half years away, to a stadium that still isn't finished.

tracks.room: Outside the museum · near its door, out of the way, with the round Palau Blaugrana beside it
tracks.title: Outside the museum · A museum in the old ice rink
tracks.where: Near the museum's door but out of the way of people going in, with the long building with the ridged roof in front of you and the round Palau Blaugrana beside it.
tracks.what: The museum building = the Palau de Gel, the club's ice rink, opened 1971 (G88 OK OFF [GO33]); closed 2022 (ROUTE §1.4, A.2 SEC NHL.com: here "When the rink closed", no year); the old museum under the main stand closed on the old stadium's last day, 28 May 2023 (F6.16 OK OFF; F16.3); this one opened to the public on 7 June 2023 ("ten days later"), about 2,400 m² (F16.11, F17.3, G105 OK OFF); meant to stay until 2024/25 (G88 OFF; "a season or two"), slipped; the skaters' new provisional rink on university land, 2026 (ROUTE §1.4 SEC ×2, DATED, separate sentence); the Palau Blaugrana opened 1971, home to the professional basketball, handball, roller hockey and futsal teams, some shirts retired there (G87 OK OFF [GO32]); a new arena planned elsewhere on the campus (ROUTE §1.4 SEC, DATED, separate sentence). Ending: football is not the only sport (fact).
tracks.listen: Why the club's museum is in an old ice rink, and what the round arena beside it is for.

tracks.room: Outside the museum · by the door or in the queue; needs no view
tracks.title: Outside the museum · Extra · The ad with two spelling mistakes
tracks.where: By the museum's door or in the queue for the ticket check, if there is one; nothing to look at.
tracks.what: The ad: 22 Oct 1899, "Miscellaneous" section at the back of the weekly (named in speech only as "a Barcelona sports weekly": see notes), "Our friend and colleague Mr Kans Kamper, of the foot-vall section", "former Swiss champion", "to organise some games in Barcelona", "Tuesday or Friday evenings between 9 and 11" (F1.3–1.5, Q1 re-checked OFF [O10]); placed with his compatriot Walter Wild (F1.6, [O10]); Hans Gamper of Winterthur, born 22 Nov 1877, so 22 a week before the meeting (G19 SEC GEC, our arithmetic), in Barcelona since "the late 1890s" (G20, lead's decision), always used the Catalan form Joan (F4.8 OK OFF); founding meeting 29 Nov 1899, Solé gymnasium off the Rambla, twelve men from Switzerland, England, Germany, Catalonia and elsewhere in Spain (F1.7–1.8 OK OFF; the club's 125-years page lists Enric Ducay "from Aragon": audit FA S1, lead's decision 6); Walter Wild the first president, "unanimously named", lent his flat on Carrer Princesa, played ten matches incl. the very first, resigned 25 Apr 1901 to leave for England (G23–G24 OK OFF, re-read); Gamper did not want to be the first president, he wanted to play (G22, GEC re-read); the city's name (F1.10 OK OFF). Ending (FACTS §22 Gamper): a club named for its city, by men from somewhere else.
tracks.listen: How a misprinted small ad founded FC Barcelona, and why the founder wasn't its first president.

tracks.room: Outside the museum · same spot; needs no view until the last lines
tracks.title: Outside the museum · Extra · The colours nobody wrote down
tracks.where: The same spot by the museum's door, or still in the queue; nothing to look at until the last lines.
tracks.what: The first shirt half blue, half claret, sleeves the other way round (F3.1 OK OFF [O11]); the 1899 board minutes give no reason (F3.5 OK SEC [S6]); the club's "most likely" theory, the Merchant Taylors' School rugby kit, via the Witty brothers (F3.2 HEDGE OFF, safe wording); the Basel story as a legend, the club leaning to the school (F3.3 LEGEND); Roger Vinton: Basel plays in blue and red (F3.3 SEC [S6]); the first badge = the city's arms with a crown and a bat (F3.6 OK OFF [O19]); [RL] the oldest shirts inside (O18).
tracks.listen: Where Barça's blue and claret came from, and why nobody can say for sure.

tracks.room: The entrance hall · just inside, to one side, near the orientation map if there is one
tracks.title: The entrance hall · From under the stand to an ice rink
tracks.where: Just inside the museum, past the ticket check, to one side of the entrance hall and near the orientation map if there is one.
tracks.what: The idea of a museum in August 1928, the board proposing to put the trophies in order (F16.1 OK OFF [O4]); opened 24 Sep 1984, the stadium's 27th birthday (our link), 950 m² under the main stand (F16.2–16.3 OK OFF); 3,600 m² by 2010 (F16.4 OK OFF); nearly two million in the record year 2016 (F16.5 OK OFF [O49]); "one of the most visited museums in Catalonia", by the club's count (F16.6 HEDGE, [O49] wording); [RL] the move into the old ice rink in 2023 (F16.11 OK OFF; version-neutral); over a million visitors in 2025 (F16.8 OK OFF, DATED); a new museum being finished inside the stadium (F16.23–16.24, DATED); version-neutral founding sentence (1899, Joan Gamper); [RL] how the visit runs (O3, O20); ending: a museum waiting to move home.
tracks.listen: How the club's museum began, why it is in an old ice rink, and how the visit runs from here.

tracks.room: The wall of trophies · where you can see it whole
tracks.title: The wall of trophies · Where to start
tracks.where: At the wall of trophies, a step back from it, where you can see the whole display at once.
tracks.what: The collection on display in 2024: more than 100 football trophies, 25 from women's football, 50 from the other sections (F16.9 OK OFF [O4], re-read); the totals, DATED, each its own sentence (F12.1–12.4 OK OFF [O35], re-read): 29 Ligas, 32 Copas del Rey (first 1909–10: "the first in 1910"), 5 European Cups (the optional 16 Super Cups cut in the audit fixes); the 2025–26 Liga and Super Cup on display from May 2026 (F12.5 OK OFF [O48], DATED); second league title in a row (F12.1); the 29th Liga awarded by a 2–0 home win over Real Madrid on 10 May 2026, the first league ever clinched against them, attributed to the club (AU-S66 OFF re-read + AU-S67 SEC; DATED, cuttable). [RL] look: how the wall is laid out (O16). Ending: not all of it was won with a football (fact).
tracks.listen: How many trophies the club has, which are the newest, and how to read the wall.

tracks.room: The European Cups · in front of the five big silver cups, at the oldest if they are in order
tracks.title: The European Cups · Third time lucky
tracks.where: In front of the five big silver European Cups, by the oldest of them, from 1992, if they stand in order.
tracks.what: Two lost European Cup finals before 1992: Benfica 1961 in Bern, 3–2, the woodwork hit four times, "the goalposts were square at the time" (F7.18 OK OFF; G62 OK OFF, re-read), and Steaua 1986 on penalties (F7.18, [O37] re-read); version-neutral: Cruyff back as coach since 1988 built the Dream Team (F7.7, F7.19 OK OFF); Wembley, 20 May 1992, Sampdoria, no goals in ninety minutes, Koeman's free kick past Pagliuca late in extra time (F7.15 OK OFF; F7.16/G44: never a minute); then Alexanko, the captain, on for Guardiola, and he lifted the cup (club 763941: "al sustituir Guardiola en el minuto 113"; audit FA M1, lead's decision 3); "Salid y disfrutad", attributed to the club's own history card, then "go out and enjoy it" (G43 OK OFF, re-read; lead's revised decision 4, lint exception 008). The Thames story dropped (see notes: Laporta vs Gaspart conflict). [RL] look: the oldest cup, 1992 (O16). Payoff (PLAN): two finals lost, the third changed everything.
tracks.listen: How Barça lost two European Cup finals and won the third, at Wembley in 1992.

tracks.room: The European Cups · at the 2006 and 2009 cups
tracks.title: The European Cups · Six out of six
tracks.where: Still at the big silver European Cups, in front of the cups from 2006 and 2009 if they are labelled or in order.
tracks.what: 2009: six trophies out of six; the club: no other team had done it (F11.4 OK OFF [O47], attributed); Paris, 17 May 2006, 2–1 v Arsenal, Eto'o, then Belletti from Larsson's pass, coach Rijkaard, the club's second European Cup (F11.1 OK OFF [O46]; "only" dropped); 2008 Guardiola from the B team (F11.2 OK OFF [O41]); the bad start, Numancia and Racing ([O47]); Stamford Bridge, 6 May 2009, Iniesta's 93rd minute, a goal needed to reach the final (F8.12 OK OFF [O61], [O41]); the Copa, the league with a 6–2 at the Bernabéu, Rome 2–0 v Manchester United, Eto'o and Messi, the first treble by a Spanish club (F11.3 OK OFF); the two Super Cups and Abu Dhabi, 19 Dec 2009, Messi's chest in extra time (F11.4–11.5 OK OFF); fourteen of a possible nineteen trophies in four seasons (F11.6 OK OFF); [RL] the Paris and Rome cups; ending: a coach from the club's own reserves.
tracks.listen: How a team coached by the man in charge of the reserves won all six trophies it played for in one year.

tracks.room: The European Cups · at the 2011 and 2015 cups
tracks.title: The European Cups · Wembley again, then Berlin
tracks.where: Still at the big silver European Cups, in front of the cups from 2011 and 2015 if they are labelled or in order.
tracks.what: Wembley 2011: Eric Abidal, back from serious illness, lifted the cup (F8.14 OK OFF [O41]; gentle, no medical detail); 3–1 v Manchester United (F11.8 OK OFF); Berlin, 6 June 2015: 3–1 v Juventus, Rakitić early, Morata's equaliser, Luis Suárez, Neymar at the very end; coach Luis Enrique in his first season; the club's second treble (F11.9 OK SEC [S11]); the black cat at Luis Enrique's first game in charge, the treble that season (G98 OK OFF light; optional, Lead's G decision: one G detail where the track covers the person); Xavi lifted it as captain in his last match (F8.13 OK SEC [S11]); seventeen consecutive seasons played, the same run as Rexach's, later matched by Messi (club 1846462, re-read 14 Nov 2026 by the fixer: "equals the run of Xavi Hernández between 1998 and 2015 and that of Charly Rexach from 1965 to 1981"; "Neither Xavi nor Rexach can boast of scoring in each of their seasons"; no "club record" wording on the page; FACTS 8.11's "scored" is wrong: audit FA M2); [RL] the 2011 and 2015 cups; payoff "Four European Cups in ten years" (FACTS §22; Catalan News "fourth in the last 10 years").
tracks.listen: Two more European Cups: the comeback of a defender at Wembley, and a captain's last match in Berlin.

tracks.room: The women's trophies · where you can see the women's European Cups
tracks.title: The women's trophies · From a Christmas match to 91,648
tracks.where: At the women's trophies, where their European Cups are in view.
tracks.what: Christmas Day 1970, a charity match at the Camp Nou v UE Centelles, played as the Selecció Ciutat de Barcelona without the club's colours, the team not recognised by the club (F13.1 OK SEC [S20]); 1971 supporters' team, 1988 a club of its own, 26 June 2002 part of FC Barcelona, professional 2015 (F13.2 OK SEC); Gothenburg 2021, 4–0 v Chelsea, the club's "first ever club" claim, attributed (F13.4 OK OFF [O53]); 2023; Bilbao 2024, 2–0 v Lyon, Lyon beaten for the first time in five meetings; (Lisbon 2025 cut in the audit fixes); Oslo, 23 May 2026, 4–0 v OL Lyonnes, the fourth title (F13.7 OK OFF-UEFA, DATED); the crowds: 91,553 v Real Madrid, 30 March 2022, then 91,648 v Wolfsburg 23 days later, world records for women's football (F6.13 OK OFF [O33], DATED wording "had seen"); Alexia from Levante at 18 in 2012, left in May 2026 as the record scorer (F13.9 OK OFF [O52], DATED); Aitana "a product of the youth team" (F13.13 OK OFF [O54]); "five times between them as Barça players, and Alexia added a third this October" (F12.9 safe wording, DATED); [RL] the four European trophies, the first fifty years after 1970 (25 Dec 1970 → 16 May 2021: audit FA S2); ending Q7.
tracks.listen: How the women's team went from a match without the club's colours to four European titles and the biggest crowds the women's game had seen.

tracks.room: The wall of shirts · where you can see the wall whole
tracks.title: The wall of shirts · The shirt that paid to be worn
tracks.where: In front of the wall of shirts, standing back far enough to see it whole.
tracks.what: 107 years with no sponsor's name across the front (F14.7 OK OFF-UN [P3]: "no commercial logo"; kit makers' marks appeared before 2006, so never "no logo, nothing": audit FA S4, lead's decision 5; the UN's "first time … a logo" stays, attributed); Levski Sofia (F14.8) dropped: the one SEC page dates it ambiguously; September 2006, UNICEF's name, and Barça paying UNICEF, not the reverse (F14.7; F18.18; no sum, decision 8); a five-year partnership ([P3]); "commercial sponsors followed" (F14.9 HEDGE safe wording); Spotify on the shirt from 2022 and the stadium's name from that summer, Spotify Camp Nou (F14.10 OK OFF [O27]); the members' assembly ratified the deal (F14.4, one clause); DATED: the name secured until 2034, the shirt to 2030 (F14.11 OK OFF [O28]); [RL] the oldest shirt with a clean front, the first UNICEF shirt if shown (O18); payoff as PLAN.
tracks.listen: Why Barça's shirt stayed clean for a century, and why, when a name finally went on it, the club paid for the privilege.

tracks.room: Cruyff's display · wherever Johan Cruyff's shirt or photographs are shown
tracks.title: Cruyff's display · A name the registrar refused
tracks.where: At the display given to Johan Cruyff, wherever his shirt or his photographs are shown in the history space.
tracks.what: Jordi Cruyff's own words, "My birth date was decided because of a Real Madrid vs. Barcelona game" (G40 HEDGE, ESPN re-read; who decided not said: lead); signed 13 Aug 1973 ("in August 1973"), the wait caused by the Dutch federation's 1–31 July window, never a Spanish rule (G33, G35 OK OFF, re-read; F18 new error); first competitive game 28 Oct 1973 v Granada, 4–0, two goals; Barça "second from bottom"; "the first of 26 games unbeaten"; the 1973–74 Liga, first in fourteen years (G36 OK OFF re-read; F7.3); Jordi born 9 Feb 1974 in Amsterdam by planned caesarean, eight days before the Bernabéu (G40, AU224 / Ara; F7.4); 0–5 on 17 Feb 1974, Cruyff the second goal (G37 OK OFF re-read); Asensi's line and Cruyff's "people were saying thank you" (G38, G39 OK OFF, re-read); the registrar wanted "Jorge", the reply about the Dutch passport (G41, Jordi's account, ESPN re-read, attributed and paraphrased); Jordi = Catalan George, patron saint (AU221; G41); Catalan names registrable from January 1977, Ley 17/1977 (AU227 fix, AU-S82 OFF BOE, via AUDIT). Not used: the fee; the volley v Atlético (left out for length); "the name was outlawed". Ending: a Catalan name, insisted on by a Dutchman (fact).
tracks.listen: How Johan Cruyff's arrival, a five–nil in Madrid and his son's name became one story.

tracks.room: Cruyff's display · same place
tracks.title: Cruyff's display · The coach who changed the club
tracks.where: Still at the display given to Johan Cruyff, near the Dream Team's photographs or shirts if they are shown.
tracks.what: Self-contained intro (E skips 013): Cruyff a star here as a player in the 1970s (F7.1–7.3); back as coach in 1988, "put into motion the best era in the history of the club" (F7.7–7.8 OK OFF, re-read [O34], attributed); four Ligas in a row 1990–91 to 1993–94, the Cup Winners' Cup, the first European Cup in 1992 (F7.9 OK OFF, re-read; one clause, 008 home); "Cruyff gave birth to the idea that today defines Barça" and "his confidence in the blaugrana youth system" (G47 OFF [GO15], re-read, attributed); left in 1996 after disagreements with Núñez (F7.7 re-read); [quietly] died 24 March 2016 of lung cancer, in Barcelona (F7.10, G47 re-read); the Clásico of 2 April 2016: "Gràcies Johan" mosaic, applause in the 14th minute for "Cruyff's famous number" (AU246 fix; second source found: OFF 2016 review, re-read; "his old number" not said: the club's own words used); the Estadi Johan Cruyff opened 2019 for the second team, the women and the under-19s (F7.13 OK OFF re-read); statue "stood at the main stand's entrance from 2019" (F7.11, G46, decision 11, DATED, cuttable). [RL] look: the Dream Team's photographs or shirts (O12). Ending: a stadium for the young players named after him (fact).
tracks.listen: What Johan Cruyff built as Barça's coach, and how the club and its fans said goodbye.

tracks.room: The Masia display · where La Masia's photographs or story are shown
tracks.title: The Masia display · The farmhouse that drew the stadium
tracks.where: At the display given to La Masia, the club's academy, where the farmhouse's photographs or its story are shown.
tracks.what: La Masia de Can Planes, a farmhouse built in 1702 (F9.1 OK OFF, re-read); first "taller para la confección de la maqueta" and "a work area for architects and builders" (F9.3 OK OFF, re-read on both pages); came with the land bought in 1950 (F9.2, re-read); then the club's headquarters (F9.3; AU-S40); a residence from 20 Oct 1979 (F9.4, re-read); about 60 boys, 12 in the farmhouse and 48 under the Gol Nord (F9.5, re-read); the stadium "visible to them through their bedroom windows" (F9.6, re-read); Iniesta at 12, leaving his family "one of the worst days I have experienced" (AU-S76 OFF, re-read); the residence left the farmhouse in 2011; the new one at the training ground for 83 (F9.4, F9.7, re-read: "dejó de ser centro formador en 2011"; Oriol Tort "inaugurada el 20 de octubre de 2011", "83 deportistas"); the club names Xavi, Iniesta and Messi (F9.8, re-read); 2010 World Cup final: "Seven of the eight were starters" (AU-S43 OFF, re-read; "six from the academy" not said: G did not confirm); to become the social headquarters, "the building has to return to its original state" (F9.9 DATED, re-read). [RL] look: the farmhouse in the photographs (O12). Payoff (PLAN).
tracks.listen: How the farmhouse where the stadium's model was made became the home of the club's academy.

tracks.room: The Més que un club display · at the club's values and identity display, or any quiet spot in the history space; needs no view until the last lines
tracks.title: The Més que un club display · Words older than the man
tracks.where: At the display on the club's values and identity, or any quiet spot in the history space; you need nothing to look at until a club crest in the last lines.
tracks.what: 17 Jan 1968, Narcís de Carreras's inauguration speech, in Catalan (F3.18, [O20] "delivered in Catalan"): official English "Barcelona is more than a football club." / "Barcelona is more than a place of leisure where we go to watch the team play every Sunday." ([O23] re-read), then our paraphrase of the official Spanish continuation "más que todas las cosas, es un espíritu que llevamos muy arraigado dentro" (G29, re-read [GO6]); the April 1933 bulletin, "much more than a mere football club" ([O23] re-read; ES "algo más que un simple club de fútbol"); 1973 advertising campaign (F3.20); Més que un club glossed; under Franco: the Castilian name, Club de Fútbol Barcelona, 1941 (F3.10, [O20]); FCB → CFB and two of the four bars removed; four bars back in 1949 for the 50th anniversary; the 1910 letters back in late 1974 ([O19] re-read); Elena Fort, institutional vice-president, Aug 2026: "Barça is more than a club because it represents a country" (Q8 re-read [O17], her words; the rest of her sentence, on Sunyol, left out: 019 home); the "other reading" sentence dropped (G gave no sourced line); 1 Oct 2017 out (decision 5). Last lines [RL]: the crest's elements (F3.8, [O19] re-read). Ending: the bars they took off and put back (fact).
tracks.listen: Where the club's motto, more than a club, really comes from, and what the crest went through under Franco.

tracks.room: A quiet corner · a bench, the rest area or any spot out of the flow
tracks.title: A quiet corner · Extra · Backsides on a wall
tracks.where: Any bench, rest area or quiet corner out of the flow of visitors, after the history displays and away from the loud screens; nothing needs to be in view until the last lines.
tracks.what: Four grounds in the club's first ten years, one where the Hospital de Sant Pau stands (F2.1–2.2 OK OFF); the Carrer de la Indústria ground, today's Carrer de París, opened March 1909 with a stand (F2.3 OK OFF); culers from cul, backside: the club's own explanation of the row of backsides on the wall (F2.5 LEGEND/OFF tradition), first a jibe, then worn with pride (F2.6 OK OFF); the doubt: a writer using the name Roger Vinton found only one photograph (F2.7 HEDGE SEC).
tracks.listen: How Barça's fans came to call themselves culers, the club's own story of a wall of backsides, and the writer who doubts it.

tracks.room: A quiet corner · same place
tracks.title: A quiet corner · Extra · The whistle that closed the club
tracks.where: The same bench or quiet corner as the story before, sitting or leaning out of the flow; nothing needs to be in view.
tracks.what: Sunday 14 June 1925, Les Corts, a friendly v CE Júpiter in tribute to the Orfeó Català (F4.1 OK OFF); at half time British sailors' band played the Spanish anthem, most of the 14,000 whistled and booed, then applauded God Save the King (F4.2 OK OFF); 24 June the civil governor under Primo de Rivera suspended the club, six months decreed (F4.3 OK OFF; F18.17: never "six months" as served); Gamper, president five times (F4.6 OK OFF), came to Barcelona in the late 1890s (GAPS change to F1.1), forced out and barred, "temporarily exiled to Switzerland" (F4.4 HEDGE OFF, the club's words); 1908 "Barcelona cannot die and must not die" (F4.7, Q2 re-checked); his death in 1930, "probably" business problems and the closure (F4.5 OK OFF, gentle); the club's centenary article of 14 June 2025 (O15). Ending: "cannot die" (FACTS §22 Gamper).
tracks.listen: The afternoon in 1925 when a crowd's whistles got the club closed and its founder forced out, and the words he had once used to save it.

tracks.room: A quiet corner · same place
tracks.title: A quiet corner · Extra · The president who never came back
tracks.where: The same bench or quiet corner, sitting or leaning out of the flow; nothing needs to be in view.
tracks.what: 6 August 1936, three weeks into the Civil War: Josep Sunyol drove from Madrid to the Guadarrama front to visit Republican troops, crossed the front line near the Alto del León pass into Nationalist-held ground, was identified and shot without trial (F4.11 OK OFF); with a journalist, a militia lieutenant and their driver (F4.12 OK OFF); born Barcelona 1898, elected by acclamation in 1935 (F4.9; Lead's decision 6: "in 1935"), owner of the weekly La Rambla, which spread the motto "sport and citizenship" (F4.10 OK OFF), a leader of Esquerra Republicana de Catalunya, member of the Spanish parliament (F4.9 OK OFF [O17]); Barcelona did not know for about a week, remains never found despite searches in 2010 and 2022 (F4.13 OK OFF); "absent president" from late 1937 (F4.14 OK OFF); "shot by Franco's troops", once (F4.15); the 1996 plaque at Guadarrama and the club's flowers on 6 Aug 2026 (F4.16 OK OFF, DATED). The presidential box: CUT (no second source in FACTS_GAPS; Lead's decision 6 and decisions after FACTS_GAPS). Ending: his motto (FACTS §22 Sunyol).
tracks.listen: The club president who drove to the front in the first weeks of the Civil War and was never seen again, and the motto he left behind.

tracks.room: A quiet corner · same place
tracks.title: A quiet corner · Extra · Eleven–one
tracks.where: Same quiet corner or bench as the last stories, away from the screens; nothing to look at.
tracks.what: 13 June 1943, Madrid, cup semi-final second leg, Real Madrid 11–1 Barcelona, 8–0 at half time; first leg 3–0 to Barça at Les Corts (F4.19 OK SEC; Goal [S9] re-read; Real Madrid [GP1] re-read); Ya's accusation (Q10, [S8] re-read: "whistled at the Madrid players with the clear intention of attacking the representatives of Spain"); Madrid fans "given free whistles upon entrance to the ground" ([S8] re-read; attributed to a Guardian writer); the dressing-room claim, the players' account (F4.21 LEGEND; [S8] "Spain's director of state security visited their dressing room"); Barau, "were overcome by military pressure" (Q9 re-read [S9]) and his own "a story that nobody has ever been able to prove", which the Goal page applies to the half-time threat, not to the pre-kick-off visit ([S9], paraphrased; audit FA S3); Barça finished with ten men (F4.23, [S9]); Real Madrid's own history: "una extraordinaria remontada", "Aquí nació la eterna rivalidad entre ambos clubes" (G1 OFF-RM, re-read; our translation); the even-handed close (G4); Franco's three honours from the club and the members' 2019 vote to withdraw them (G14 OFF, re-read [GO3]; the lead's optional balance sentence, no years for the honours). Not used: the Guardian's "some Madridistas question…" line (the page applies it to a detail, not to the visit: see notes); Di Stéfano (lead: out). Last lines: both cities still tell it differently.
tracks.listen: The most argued-over match in the club's history, and what each side says about it.

tracks.room: Messi's space · at its way in, out of the flow
tracks.title: Messi's space · A promise on a paper napkin
tracks.where: At the way in to Messi's space, the room with his golden balls, standing to one side out of the flow of visitors.
tracks.what: A thirteen-year-old from Rosario with a hormone deficiency that held back his growth; no club would guarantee the treatment (F10.6 OK SEC, gentle, no figures); the trial in September 2000 and Rexach's walk round the pitch, three or four minutes that took fifteen (AU298 fix, AU-S75 SEC, his account); "Sign him. Don't even think about it" to the coaches beside him (AU §3.9, AU-S75, re-checked); the napkin of 14 December 2000 at a tennis club, the story goes (F10.1 OK SEC; F10.2 HEDGE), "under his sole responsibility" (re-checked, Ara's English), Minguella and Gaggioli as witnesses, a moral promise, not a contract (F10.3 OK SEC); sold at auction in 2024, not in this museum (F10.4 HEDGE SEC; F10.5; lint two-sentence form); at thirteen he crossed the Atlantic and joined the under-14s (F10.7 OK OFF). Ending: a promise on a napkin, kept.
tracks.listen: How a boy from Rosario was promised a future at Barça on a paper napkin, and why the napkin isn't here.

tracks.room: Messi's space · where the golden balls are in view
tracks.title: Messi's space · Six won here, eight on show
tracks.where: Inside Messi's space, standing where you can see his row of golden balls and the Golden Boots beside them.
tracks.what: Six Ballons d'Or won as a Barça player, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2019; eight in all (F10.16 OK OFF; F18.8); version-neutral "He came from Rosario as a boy and played here until 2021" (H skips 021, 023); the Ballon d'Or glossed once; the museum shows all eight, the eighth his gift in 2024 (F10.17 HEDGE SEC: never "originals"); six European Golden Shoes (F10.13 OK OFF; F16.17 OK OFF: the Golden Boots shown); 672 goals in 778 matches, more than Pelé's 643 for Santos (F10.9, F10.11 OK OFF); 91 goals in 2012, beating Gerd Müller's 1972 (F10.13); thirty-five major trophies (F10.10); Q14 attributed (OFF [O3]); the club's count of twelve men's Ballons d'Or, from Luis Suárez, the first Spanish-born winner, in 1960 (GAPS G67–G69; Lead's decisions after FACTS_GAPS; past tense), level with Real Madrid by the club's count (F12.7 OK OFF [O36]). Payoff.
tracks.listen: Messi's golden balls, which six of them he won in Barça's colours, and the numbers behind them.

tracks.room: Messi's space · same place, or by his shirts if shown
tracks.title: Messi's space · The boy from Rosario
tracks.where: Still in Messi's space, by the golden balls or, if they are shown, by his shirts, out of the flow of visitors.
tracks.what: Official debut 16 October 2004 v Espanyol, a city derby, at the Olympic stadium on Montjuïc, a one–nil win, aged seventeen (F10.8 OK OFF; AU §3.4: never at the Camp Nou; age our arithmetic from 24 June 1987, AU-S44); a friendly at sixteen at the opening of Porto's new stadium (F10.8, optional); the Getafe goal, April 2007, Camp Nou, cup semi-final, from his own half past five players after Xavi's pass, "Maradona-esque" (AU321–322 OK, AU-S48 OFF, attributed); 46 goals at the Camp Nou in 2011–12 (F10.14 OK OFF, optional); 5 August 2021: agreement reached but "cannot be formalised due to economic and structural obstacles" (F10.15 OK SEC; Q12 re-checked); the league's spending rules (AU329 OK, AU-S47; Al Jazeera's own explanation); tears at the farewell three days later (AU334, AU-S46 SEC); Paris Saint-Germain; the No 10 to Ansu Fati, then Lamine Yamal since July 2025 (AU339 fix, AU-S45 SEC, DATED, cuttable). Ending: the number handed on (FACTS §22 Messi).
tracks.listen: Messi's first official game, the goal people compare to Maradona's, the summer he had to leave, and who wears his number now.

tracks.room: The round room · at its way in, out of the flow, before going in
tracks.title: The round room · Before the show
tracks.where: At the way in to the round room with the screens, where the exhibition ends, standing to one side out of the flow, before you go in.
tracks.what: The club's warning first: the immersive room is not recommended for people with epilepsy or photosensitivity; the club asks them to tell the tour staff, who will guide them (F16.19 OK OFF [O58]; OFF accessibility page re-read); the show has its own sound: stop this guide while it plays (decision 5); the official description only: a double-height round room, its walls one screen, 78 m long and 6 m high (F16.13 OK OFF [O4]); the club calls it the largest immersive room in a sports museum in Europe (F16.12, attributed); the show is called Spotify Camp Nou Live and places you at the centre of the stadium; the exhibition culminates here (F16.14 OK OFF [O6], [O58]). Nothing on the show's content or length (O11).
tracks.listen: The club's one warning for the round room, what the room is, and when to stop and restart this guide.

tracks.room: The round room · just outside it, or inside once the show ends, out of the way
tracks.title: The round room · After the show: the first full house
tracks.where: Just outside the round room, or inside it once the show has ended, standing out of the way of people coming and going.
tracks.what: The show's official framing only (F16.14: at the centre of the stadium); 24 September 1957, La Mercè, the city's feast day: opening day (F5.15 OK OFF [O25]); morning Mass, a statue of the Virgin of Montserrat, Handel's Hallelujah, only about half the seats filled (O25 re-read); afternoon packed, a parade of Catalan clubs with Espanyol at the back, sardanas, about eleven thousand white doves (F5.15); the Spanish flag raised and the national anthem, the stadium standing: Franco's Spain (F5.16 OK OFF, even-handed); 4–2 v a team billed as a Warsaw eleven (F5.17; F18.13: never "Legia"); more than ninety thousand, works unfinished (F5.18; F5.19 safe wording); first goal after eleven minutes, Eulogio Martínez (F5.17 OK OFF [O26]); optional: Eulogio first to score five in a game there, 1960 (GAPS G96 OK OFF, one G detail on a person the track covers). Ending: the first goal in a stadium that would see thousands (no number).
tracks.listen: The day the stadium opened in 1957: a Mass, eleven thousand doves, the flag and anthem of the day, and the first goal.

tracks.room: The models · where you can see the model of the finished stadium whole
tracks.title: The models · The stadium when it's finished
tracks.where: At the models of the future stadium, standing where you can see the big model of the finished stadium whole, roof and all. If the models are elsewhere or gone, play it wherever the route reaches the stadium first.
tracks.what: The lower two tiers of 1957 kept and renovated, the third tier taken down and rebuilt (F15.3 OK OFF-supplier [P1]); about 105,000 when finished (F15.13 OK OFF, DATED); a cable-held tensile roof over every fan, close to fifty thousand square metres, "one of the largest tensile structures in the world" per the club's stadium site, 18,000 m² of solar panels (F15.12 HEDGE OFF [O57]); the new facade inspired by the 1957 canopy of Mitjans, Soteras and García, the old inner canopy to disappear (F15.14 OK OFF [O9]); the double VIP ring and up to 25 ha of car-free grounds (F15.15 OK OFF [O57]); Nikken Sekkei with b720 Fermín Vázquez, contractor Limak (F15.1 OK OFF, F15.2 OK OFF-supplier); the new museum in the Tribuna hub facing the Campus esplanade (F16.23 OK OFF, DATED).
tracks.listen: What the finished stadium will be, who is building it, and why the 1957 bowl is still inside it.

tracks.room: The models · same place, or any spot nearby
tracks.title: The models · Nobody owns Barça
tracks.where: Still at the models of the future stadium, or at any spot nearby out of the way of the people coming through.
tracks.what: Member ownership: one of four Spanish professional clubs still owned by their members, with Real Madrid, Athletic Club and Osasuna; members elect the president by direct vote (F14.1 OK SEC [S25], 2014, attributed); 151,787 members at 30 Jun 2026 (G81 OK OFF, DATED); about 1,270 official penyes on all five continents (G82 OK OFF, DATED count); the land for the 1957 stadium bought after the club's first-ever referendum (F5.9 OK OFF [O20]); first elections after Franco, 6 May 1978 (F14.6, F4.26 OK OFF); 19 Dec 2021 referendum on financing the works, the biggest referendum turnout ever (F14.3 OK OFF [O55]; no percentage, no sum); the Spotify deal ratified 625–49 by the delegates' assembly (F14.4 OK OFF [O27]); 15 Mar 2026 election: 114,504 entitled, about 48,440 voted, Laporta re-elected (F14.2 OK OFF [O51], DATED); Sept 2026 assembly approved new financing to finish the stadium (F14.5 OK OFF [O29], DATED).
tracks.listen: Who owns Barça, and the votes that decided this stadium, its shirt and its president.

tracks.room: The viewpoint · at the rail, the stadium in view
tracks.title: The viewpoint · What you're looking at
tracks.where: At the rail of the Construction Viewpoint, the balcony over the stadium works, with the bowl in front of you. If it is crowded, step back to any spot with a view of the stands.
tracks.what: Back in use since 22 Nov 2025 (F15.6 OK OFF [O7]); the lower two tiers are the 1957 bowl, kept and renovated (F15.3 OK OFF-supplier [P1]); the top ring built but not yet open (F15.10 OK SEC, DATED); the 830-metre compression ring at the very top completed on 5 Oct 2026 (ROUTE §4, SEC Ara 10 Oct 2026, DATED); more than 3,000 reinforcement jobs on the old second tier against about 800 planned (F15.16 OK OFF [O29]); about 62,000 seats in use (F15.9 OK SEC [S3], [S4], DATED); the roof from next summer, built on the pitch and lifted on cables, the team back to Montjuïc for a few months (F15.11 DATED SEC [S7], [S4]; Ara 10 Oct 2026); Q13, the treasurer's words (CA, SEC [S7], re-checked); about 105,000 when finished (F15.13 OK OFF, DATED).
tracks.listen: What you can see of the stadium today, what was kept, what was rebuilt, and what still has to happen.

tracks.room: The old benches · sitting on the original benches from the old stadium, the bowl in view
tracks.title: The old benches · Where the players sat
tracks.where: On the original benches from the old stadium, at the viewpoint, with the bowl in view. If they are full, stand beside them, out of the way.
tracks.what: The benches from the old stadium, put here so visitors can sit where the club's legendary players sat (F17.4 OK OFF [O50], DATED); the 1982 World Cup opening ceremony and first game (F6.2 OK OFF [O26]); 7 Nov 1982, John Paul II's Mass before 120,000, the first papal Mass in Catalonia, some words in Catalan to an exceptionally silent stadium (F6.5 OK OFF [O31]); his membership card, in his own words of 14 May 1999 (G101 OK OFF-Holy See; no number); 8 Aug 1992 Olympic final, Spain 3–2 Poland, Kiko in the last minute, Guardiola and Albert Ferrer (F6.9 OK OFF [O32]); Spain's first Olympic football gold (F6.10 as corrected by G51); Paris 2024 with Fermín López, Eric Garcia and Pau Cubarsí (G51–G52 OK OFF, cuttable); 26 May 1999 Champions League final, Basler for Bayern, then Sheringham and Solskjær in the dying seconds (F6.11 OK OFF-UEFA [P5]); the women's world-record crowds of 2022, one clause (F6.13 OK OFF [O33]).
tracks.listen: The benches the players sat on, and the nights the stadium belonged to the whole city and the world, not only the club.

tracks.room: The old benches · sitting; needs no view until the last lines
tracks.title: The old benches · Extra · The stadium the nickname named
tracks.where: On the old benches at the viewpoint, or anywhere quiet nearby; nothing to look at until the last lines, which need the bowl in view.
tracks.what: The official name Estadi del FC Barcelona, endorsed by a 1965 referendum; everyone said "camp nou", the new ground; in 2000–01, 68.25% of members voted to make Camp Nou official (F5.21 OK OFF [O25]); Les Corts opened 20 May 1922 v St Mirren, 2–1, ready three months after the first stone, 22,000, then "tens of thousands, and still not enough" (F2.9 OK OFF [O13], [O12]; F2.10 as corrected by G60); the site changed twice before Miró-Sans, elected 1953, settled it (F5.8 OK OFF [O26]); his slogan (G65 OK OFF [GO20], as relayed, re-checked); first stone 28 Mar 1954 before 60,000 (F5.10 OK OFF [O26]); architects Mitjans, Soteras and García-Barbón, Mitjans the president's cousin (F5.11–5.12 OK OFF [O26], [O25], [O9]); more than four times the estimate, debt blamed for lean years (F5.13 OK OFF; our arithmetic 288/66.6); the lower tiers are 1957's (F15.3).
tracks.listen: How the stadium got its name, from a ground too small, a site that moved twice and a bill four times the estimate.

tracks.room: The old benches · same place
tracks.title: The old benches · Extra · The refugee signed at half past eight
tracks.where: Still sitting on the old benches at the viewpoint, the stadium in view; nothing to look at until the last lines.
tracks.what: 15 June 1950, 8.30 pm, right after a friendly at Sarrià against Espanyol (F5.1 OK OFF, re-read [O24]); Samitier, 1920s star, technical secretary (F5.1, F8.1); Hungaria, footballers who had fled behind the Iron Curtain; "a political refugee being pursued by the Hungarian federation" (F5.2, re-read, attributed); no competitive matches until the 1951 cup ("at first": date dropped for the date count); brother-in-law Daučík (F5.4, re-read); Ladislau (F19); 10 Feb 1952, 9–0 v Sporting Gijón, seven goals, equalling the Liga record set by Bata against Barça in 1931, "has never been touched since" ([O60] re-read; DATED, separate sentence, F18.40); Daučík: "Kubala scored goals today, but he didn't have a great game." (Q6, re-read); the Five Cups of 1951–52: Liga, Spanish Cup, Latin Cup, Copa Eva Duarte, Copa Martini Rossi (G64 OK OFF, re-read; lead's decision); the club: not built because of him, "the plans to build the new ground were already in place some time before he signed in 1950", "Kubala did generate unprecedented interest" (F5.6, [O25] re-read; lint exception 031); Les Corts "tens of thousands, and still not enough" (lead's decision; [GO20] "The Club needed a bigger stadium"); statue "stood at the main stand's entrance from 2009", by Montserrat Garcia Rius (F5.7, G48, decision 11; DATED, cuttable; position never cued). Last lines [RL]; payoff (PLAN).
tracks.listen: How a Hungarian refugee became Barça's great star, and why the stadium was not built for him.

tracks.room: The old benches · same place
tracks.title: The old benches · Extra · Three and a half thousand voices
tracks.where: Still on the old benches at the viewpoint, or anywhere quiet nearby; the last lines need the bowl in view.
tracks.what: The Cant del Barça first performed at the stadium on 27 Nov 1974 for the 75th anniversary; words by Jaume Picas and Josep Maria Espinàs, music by Manuel Valls (F3.13 OK OFF [O22], [O21]); some three and a half thousand singers from 78 choirs, conducted by Oriol Martorell (F3.14 HEDGE, safe wording; [O22]); the same evening, songs banned under Franco, the Cant de la Senyera sung there for the first time (F3.16 HEDGE OFF, re-checked on [O22]); a year before Franco died (F4.26 OK OFF [O20]); the board of those years put Catalan back on the stadium's public address (F3.22 OK OFF [O20]); what the song says, in our words (Lead's decision 17); no lyrics.
tracks.listen: The night the club's anthem was first sung in the stadium, and the songs that came back with it.

tracks.room: The old benches · same place
tracks.title: The old benches · Extra · Nine days before
tracks.where: Still sitting on the old benches at the viewpoint; nothing to look at, the story ends on two nights in Madrid.
tracks.what: Maradona signed 4 June 1982, "the world most expensive footballer" (F8.3 OK OFF, [O30] re-read); nine days later the World Cup opened in this stadium, Belgium 1–0 Argentina, the world champions (F6.2 OK OFF; F6.3 SEC [S10]; F6.4: our linking); scored in his first official game, a 2–1 defeat to Valencia; hepatitis December 1982 ([O30] re-read); 1983: the Copa del Rey (2–1, Zaragoza) and the Copa de la Liga over two legs, both against Real Madrid ([O30] re-read); 26 June 1983, Copa de la Liga at the Bernabéu: "dribbled past Agustín and watched as Juan José crashed into the post", "The Real Madrid fans stood to applaud Maradona's goal" (G63 OK OFF, re-read; lead's revised decision 7); the ankle injury from Goikoetxea's challenge; the 1984 cup final against Athletic, the "battle on the field", a three-month ban, Napoli that summer ([O30] re-read; neutral, no blame); 38 goals in 58 matches ([O30]); 19 Nov 2005: 3–0 at the Bernabéu, Eto'o after 14 minutes from "a pass from debutante Messi", Ronaldinho 59' and 77', "a standing ovation by the Madrid fans at the final whistle", Messi's first Clásico (F8.10 OK OFF, [O39] re-read). Not used: the 1974 0–5 and Asensi (013 home); "the rarest honour". Payoff (PLAN).
tracks.listen: Maradona's short, wild time at Barça, and the two nights the Bernabéu stood up for a Barça player.

tracks.room: The way out · at the exit, or just outside it, out of the way
tracks.title: The way out · A club that keeps coming home
tracks.where: At the exit of the visit, or just outside it, out of the way of people leaving. If the way out is back past the viewpoint, play it there before you leave.
tracks.what: Recap, every clause self-contained and version-neutral: the misspelled advert of 1899 (F1.3–1.4 OK OFF); the 1925 closure after the crowd whistled an anthem, the founder lost, his promise that the club could not die (F4.2–4.7 OK OFF; no quote, 018 home); a Dutchman who taught it a way of playing (F7.7 OK OFF); boys who slept under a stand (F9.5 OK OFF); a promise to Messi on a napkin (F10.1 OK SEC); the women's world-record crowds (F6.13 OK OFF). The homes: four grounds in ten years (F2.1 OK OFF), Carrer de la Indústria in 1909 (F2.3), Les Corts in 1922 (F2.9), the Camp Nou in 1957 (F5.15), two seasons at Montjuïc (F15.5 OK OFF [O29]), a museum in the old ice rink (F16.11 OK OFF), one more spell away when the roof goes on (F15.11 DATED SEC). Payoff answering 001's title line. No store, no plug.
tracks.listen: A last look back at a club that has moved house again and again, and always come home.
